comment: The nested-routine and doc-example families, pinned in both directions. POSITIVE: a named nested routine is published with `scope` set to its parent and is the far end of a `contains` edge, so the `calls` edges the analyzer already emitted have a symbol to land on; a `runnableExamples` block's TYPE declarations are published and yield real `extends` edges. NEGATIVE: an unnamed nested routine stays suppressed (it is the anonymous inner body entity the family rule is about), a doc example's VALUE declarations stay suppressed (they are locals of the example, not of the module — `LocalsAreNotSymbols`), and a doc example must not leak a `contains` edge from the routine that documents it. The `contains` forbid is the half that catches a 'helpful' fix which routed the nested routine through `ownerName`, because the owner here is a FUNCTION and `ownerName` is the family field for a class owner.

expectRelationships.comment: the lexical containment of a named nested routine. Read off `metadata.nimNestedIn` and NOT from `ownerName`, because the owner is a function here and `ownerName` is the family field for a class or module owner
the parent calling the closure by name — the edge that used to have no symbol at its far end
a `runnableExamples` block's type declaration is a declaration the Nim compiler type-checks, so it yields the same edge as a module-scope one
an object FIELD is contained by its owner — published the same way whether the object is module-scope or inside a doc example, which is the control for the example's own members
the second named nested routine, so the family is pinned by two independent sites rather than one

PARENLESS UFCS of a NESTED routine: `s.trimmed` invokes `trimmed(s)` with no parentheses and no call node. Confidence 0.9 because the dispatch is inferred from a member read plus a declaration, not written as a call

forbidSymbols.name: s
forbidSymbols.comment: a doc example's `var s = Circle()` is a local of the EXAMPLE — LocalsAreNotSymbols, the same rule as a `var` in a routine body

forbidSymbols.name: label
forbidSymbols.comment: a doc example's `var label` — a local of the example unit, not of the module

forbidSymbols.name: q
forbidSymbols.comment: an UNNAMED nested routine's parameter set publishes no symbol; the routine itself has no name to publish

forbidSymbols.name: exampleOnlyLocal
forbidSymbols.comment: declared NOWHERE else in the fixture, so this forbid is a real assertion rather than a name collision: a doc example's `var` is a local of the example unit, and publishing it as a module symbol is `LocalsAreNotSymbols` violated

forbidRelationships.comment: a doc example is NOT contained in the routine that documents it — it is a separate compilation unit, and a `contains` edge here would put a doc example inside the API surface of the proc
a self-containment edge is not a containment
`of RootObj` is the compiler's own root and is deliberately not published, so `extends` never points at a name with no referent

`runnableExamples:` is a doc-comment PRAGMA, not a call. The grammar parses the whole example as the call's argument_list, so without the shape test this published an edge to a name no Nim program can call

DELIBERATE co-existence is NOT wanted here, unlike `extends`+`references`: `s.trimmed` is a CALL and not a read, so publishing both would be the double-count. The oracle's own comment records that emitting both was a real defect it once had
